argument:
The bear's lower guided margin is a relevant normalization signal. Even its prospective 56–58% range remains above the prior-year Q2 observed 49.6%, a period comparison rather than a forecast of achieved improvement. The purchase case consequently need not require the 60.3% quarterly peak to persist. Actual Q2 FCF also rose to NT$287.36bn from NT$199.85bn despite heavy investment, supporting cash participation beyond net-income gains.

Inventory days of 87 require demand and capacity scrutiny, while cash cannot resolve Taiwan exposure. The NT$63.20bn investment gain is excluded from the recurring-growth argument. At 22x forecast earnings, the optimistic scenario is sustained operating profitability with internally funded capacity, accepting normalization and geopolitical risk rather than claiming immunity. Strong cash gives financing flexibility through that scenario; an extended price trend still favors restraint about immediate entry quality.
key_points: Lower guidance need not imply loss of all prior-year margin improvement.
Q2 post-capex cash increased despite investment intensity.
Financial resilience cannot eliminate Taiwan or inventory risk.
rebuttal_to_previous: I concede peak margins are not assured. Guided 56–58% is still above prior-year Q2 49.6%, and actual Q2 FCF increased to NT$287.36bn. These sustain a normalization-compatible purchase scenario, without treating guidance as delivered or cash as geopolitical insurance.
